items.headline: U.S. Stocks Edge Lower Amid Hawkish Fed Remarks; Tech Resilience Noted
items.summary: U.S. equities ended Friday with a cautious tone, drifting lower as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole symposium intensified expectations for a September interest rate hike. Warsh stressed the Fed's commitment to combating inflation, leading economists to now estimate a nearly 60% chance of a rate increase next month. Despite the broader market's retreat, the technology sector showed some resilience, influenced by strong earnings reports earlier in the week from major companies like NVIDIA and Salesforce, which continued to underpin investor sentiment in AI-related growth.

items.headline: Elastic Surges on Strong Earnings and Outlook
items.summary: Elastic ($ESTC) shares jumped 19% after the search and observability software company reported first-quarter results that surpassed consensus estimates and raised its full-year 2027 outlook, demonstrating robust growth in its subscription revenue.

items.headline: Affirm Holdings Rises on Strong Quarterly Performance
items.summary: Affirm Holdings ($AFRM) saw its shares climb 9% after the buy now, pay later company reported a strong fourth quarter and provided an upbeat outlook for fiscal year 2027, driven by increased gross merchandise volume and expanding operating margins.

items.headline: Gap Jumps on Q2 Results and Leadership Change
items.summary: Gap ($GAP) shares rose 15% in pre-market trading, extending gains after the retailer announced its second-quarter results and a new CEO for its Old Navy brand, signaling positive investor reaction despite mixed earnings.

items.headline: Build-A-Bear Workshop Declines Significantly
items.summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop ($BBW) was among the weakest performers, with shares plummeting 27.3% today, though specific drivers for this sharp decline were not immediately clear, highlighting vastly different investor expectations compared to high-growth stocks.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Drops Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) shares sank over 9% by midday, following an 8% drop in pre-market trading, despite the company beating earnings expectations. The decline suggests that the results fell short of investors' elevated expectations for AI-related growth and order fulfillment pace.

items.headline: PayPal Slumps Amid Acquisition Talk Abandonment
items.summary: PayPal ($PYPL) shares slumped after reports indicated that a consortium had abandoned plans for a takeover bid, leading to a significant negative reaction from investors.

items.headline: Technology Sector Shows Resilience Driven by AI Optimism
items.summary: The Information Technology sector continued to demonstrate leadership, fueled by strong demand for AI infrastructure and custom chips, with companies like Broadcom ($AVGO) and NVIDIA ($NVDA) remaining key players. This tech strength helped counter broader market caution. Communication services also posted gains.

items.headline: Industrials and Healthcare Lag, Broader Market Under Pressure
items.summary: Industrial and healthcare stocks were trading lower today, with ten of the eleven S&P 500 sectors, excluding information technology, ending in negative territory. Consumer Staples also continued to lag the broader S&P 500.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Signals Further Action on Inflation at Jackson Hole
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, emphasizing the central bank's unwavering commitment to achieving its 2% inflation target. He stated that the Fed has 'more work to do' if inflation remains elevated, prompting traders to raise the probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September to nearly 60%.

items.headline: Jobless Claims Fall, Consumer Sentiment Declines in August
items.summary: New economic data revealed that jobless claims for the week ending August 22 decreased by 4,000 to 203,000, signaling continued labor market tightness. However, consumer sentiment declined in August, with the University of Michigan's Index falling to 51.7 from 55.2 in July, despite still beating expectations. The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index for July showed a 3.7% rise, still above the Fed's target.

items.headline: Key Earnings Reports Drive Individual Stock Movements
items.summary: Salesforce ($CRM) and NVIDIA ($NVDA) reported strong earnings earlier in the week, significantly boosting investor confidence in the tech sector. Today, Elastic ($ESTC) and Affirm Holdings ($AFRM) also delivered strong quarterly results, while Marvell Technology ($MRVL) saw its stock decline despite an earnings beat, likely due to very high market expectations. Several other companies, including Frontline ($FRO), Jiayin Group ($JFIN), and MINISO Group Holding ($MNSO), were expected to report earnings today. Not financial advice.
